paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is about: the LORD keeps His word, and He is the One who hands out the land. Esau got Mount Seir, and Lot's descendants got Ar and the land of the Ammonites, and the LORD told Israel to leave all of it alone. He said Israel would not get "not even a footprint" (Deuteronomy 2:5). The notes about the Horites, the Emites and the Zamzummites show the LORD had been giving other peoples their homes long before Israel showed up (Deuteronomy 2:12, 21-22).

That matters, because Israel had a land of its own coming, and it wasn't going to get there by grabbing what belonged to somebody else. They paid in silver for the food and water along the way (Deuteronomy 2:6). The LORD's promises to you are the same kind of thing. You don't have to take what He hasn't given, and you can be generous and honest on the road while you wait for what He has.

And look at who was with them the whole time. Moses tells the people, "The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing" (Deuteronomy 2:7). Even the long wandering was under His watch, and what He swore came true (Deuteronomy 2:14). So when your own road feels long, baker, trust the One who is walking it with you. The story isn't over, because Moses still has more to say.
